name: Thunder god vine (Tripterygium wilfordii)
short: Pooled clinical studies: about 31% of users had adverse events, affecting gut, reproductive system, liver, kidney, blood and skin. Reviews describe reduced fertility and loss of periods.
text: In a quantitative synthesis of 46 clinical studies (2437 participants given Tripterygium wilfordii polyglycoside), the pooled incidence of adverse events was 30.75% and of severe adverse events 4.68%, with intestinal, reproductive, liver, kidney, blood and skin toxicity reported. A separate meta-analysis of 36 articles (2,017 participants) put the incidence of kidney toxicity at 5.81%, while noting that this might be an overestimate because of poor study quality. A review of reproductive toxicity described decreased sperm motility and fertility in men, with testicular atrophy possible after long-term use, and menstrual disorders, amenorrhea and infertility in women. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
